papers.title_en: The Collaboration Tax: How Much LLM Multi-Agent Systems Pay to Coordinate
papers.authors: Weixiang Sun, Zehong Wang, Hong Huang, Colby Nelson, Yanfang Ye
papers.evidence: 以合作博弈视角研究LLM多智能体系统的协作代价
papers.tldr: 大语言模型多智能体系统广泛部署，但两模型协作时的性能损失仍属未知。本文把协作税形式化为合作博弈中的团队去中心化损失，在32个任务、11个模型上测量。结果发现，该税沿模型类别排序且随能力单调递减，根源并非推理缺陷，而是无根据声明、不查询伙伴等四阶段对话级联。此税可从对话特征预测，且提示干预可部分消除，使协作成本成为可量化、可干预的指标。
papers.abstract_en: Multi-agent systems built from large language models are deployed widely, yet how much performance is lost when two LLMs must coordinate rather than act alone remains unclear. We formulate the collaboration tax as the team-decentralisation loss of a two-player cooperative game with private information, with two propositions characterising its sign and its equivalence to a max-superadditivity violation. We operationalise this definition on 32 solo-tractable tasks grouped by source of grounding friction and measure it on 11 models from 7 providers. The tax is structured along two no-exception axes: a category ordering across every model and a monotonic decrease with capability. The proximate mechanism is not a reasoning deficit but a four-stage conversational cascade in which agents make ungrounded claims, fail to query the partner, skip integrating both views, and accept the answer without re-derivation. The tax is mechanically predictable from conversation features and partly tractable: a prompt intervention targeting all four stages closes a substantial fraction of the gap, with the dominant bottleneck differing across categories. In heterogeneous pairs the tax is pulled toward the stronger partner rather than the additive midpoint, empirically realising the max-superadditivity violation predicted by our framework. Together these results recast collaboration in LLM systems as a measurable, predictable, and partly tractable cost.

papers.title_en: Test-Time Collaborative Classification over Multi-Agent Networks
papers.authors: Ping Hu, Mert Kayaalp, Ali H. Sayed
papers.evidence: 独立训练智能体在测试时通过分布式协议协调决策
papers.tldr: 多智能体系统的异质性使得全局联合训练困难，而测试时协作推理为分布式决策提供了新思路。本文提出一种测试时协作分类框架，各智能体独立训练后，通过交换局部决策统计量并遵循分布式学习协议来形成集体预测。理论部分建立了有限轮次、有限精度通信下的分类误差边界和PAC泛化界，揭示了模型异质性、网络拓扑、组合策略与通信约束的影响。实验结果同时展现了独立训练带来的代价与集体预测带来的收益，为异构网络中的分布式学习提供了可靠依据。
papers.abstract_en: The increasing heterogeneity of multi-agent systems poses significant challenges for jointly training a global model across agents. At the same time, cooperative inference between agents has long been recognized as a powerful mechanism for distributed decision making over networks. Motivated by these observations, we propose a collaboration framework for distributed binary classification over multi-agent networks, where a set of independently trained agents, potentially differing in architecture, feature space, or modality, coordinate their actions during test time to form collective predictions. This coordination is achieved by exchanging local decision statistics through a distributed learning protocol. We develop a theoretical and experimental study of this independent training and cooperative inference paradigm, and examine its performance under different communication budgets and distributed learning rules. We establish classification error guarantees under sufficient, finite-round, and finite-precision communication, together with PAC-style generalization bounds. These results capture the influence of model heterogeneity, network topology, combination policy, and communication constraints on prediction accuracy. Taken together with the experimental results, they reveal both the price of independent training and the benefit of collective prediction for the proposed distributed decision making framework with models learned from data.

papers.title_en: A Theoretical Framework for Parallel Lifelong MAPF Using Group Decentralized Planning
papers.authors: Alex DeWeese, Jiaoyang Li, Guannan Qu
papers.evidence: 利用多智能体MDP理论为并行终身多智能体路径规划提供分组分散规划的理论框架
papers.tldr: 终身多智能体路径规划中，RHCR框架提供高质量解但计算成本高，难以扩展至较大规模。本文在折扣MDP形式下证明RHCR近似最优，并利用局部交互MDP理论提出分组去中心化RHCR（GD-RHCR），按传递通信方案划分智能体并行规划。理论证明GD-RHCR与RHCR达到指数相近的最优保证，建立时间限制与空间划分的对偶。实验显示GD-RHCR在多种地图上保持高吞吐量，且规划成本显著降低，支持更多智能体。
papers.abstract_en: In the Lifelong Multi-Agent Path Finding (L-MAPF) problem, agents must repeatedly move from one destination to another while avoiding obstacles and inter-agent collisions. Widely regarded as one of the highest-performing solutions to this problem is the Rolling-Horizon Collision Resolution (RHCR) framework. However, commensurate with its quality solutions, it incurs a computational cost that limits its applicability to even modest agent counts. In this paper, leveraging theoretical methods from the Locally Interdependent Multi-Agent MDP literature, we first theoretically prove the near-optimality of RHCR in a discounted MDP formulation of the L-MAPF problem. Then, we leverage these results to naturally motivate an extended framework called Group Decentralized RHCR (GD-RHCR) which incorporates a group decentralized structure that partitions agents based on a transitive communication scheme and plans for each partition of agents in parallel. We show that both RHCR and GD-RHCR achieve similar exponentially close to optimal guarantees, establishing a theoretical duality between the time based restrictions performed by vanilla RHCR and the additional space based partitioning performed by GD-RHCR. Lastly, we show that across varying maps, GD-RHCR is able to attain high throughput that scales into higher agent counts while maintaining a significantly lower per plan cost.

papers.title_en: Counterfactual Quotient Models: Learning What Actions Change, Not What the World Does
papers.authors: Junlin Chen, Ruijie Wang, Jianxin Li
papers.evidence: 反事实未来建模，直接关联多智能体信用分配问题
papers.tldr: 强化学习模型常预测完整未来状态，但动作选择仅依赖动作间的差异。提出Counterfactual Quotient Model，通过居中表示去除动作共享分量，直接从同步反事实轨迹学习动作依赖效应。实验表明该方法抑制无关变异、支持新奖励查询并提升动作排序。理论证明其决策充分性、可识别性等性质。
papers.abstract_en: Reinforcement-learning models commonly predict complete future states, observations, or feature occupancies, even though action selection depends only on differences between the consequences of candidate actions. As a result, these models may devote substantial statistical and representational capacity to high-dimensional phenomena that evolve independently of the agent's current choice. We introduce the Counterfactual Quotient Model, which treats action-conditioned futures as equivalent when they differ only by a component shared across actions. Its canonical centered representation removes this common component while preserving every pairwise action comparison expressible by the modeled reward family. The implemented model learns these action-dependent effects directly from synchronized counterfactual rollouts, so shared stochastic dynamics cancel before function approximation rather than after complete futures have been predicted. We establish the decision sufficiency, identifiability, common-mode invariance, approximation behavior, and regret properties of the resulting representation. Controlled experiments in physics-based environments provide initial evidence for these properties: direct effect learning suppresses action-independent variation, supports previously unseen reward queries, and improves action ranking relative to models trained to predict absolute futures.
